insights.title: Why a full-spectrum carpentry partner is the smarter choice
insights.summary: Site carpentry and fine joinery look like two trades, but when one project splits them the cost is rework, delay and over-budget. Here is how a full-spectrum partner removes that pain.
insights.lead: Choosing a provider that runs both on-site carpentry and workshop joinery sharply cuts project risk and communication cost.

sections.title: The problem with split trades
sections.summary: Framing, fix-out and cabinetry by different subcontractors means mismatched measurements, poor sequence handover and rework cost that usually lands on the owner.

sections.title: The full-spectrum advantage
sections.summary: One team does frame measuring and cabinetry detailing, so dimensions line up; accountability is clear with no finger-pointing; program is coordinated and predictable.

sections.title: How to spot a true full-spectrum partner
sections.summary: Signs: ① own workshop and equipment; ② own site carpentry crew; ③ one complete quote (not piecemeal); ④ reference projects you can visit.

insights.title: Adelaide kitchen renovation costs: 2026 market guide
insights.summary: A kitchen reno is among the highest-return home improvements. We lay out typical Adelaide 2026 price bands and the key cost drivers so you are not over- or under-quoted.
insights.lead: Know the market and you avoid both rip-offs and too-good-to-be-true quotes. This is an objective local reference.

sections.title: Typical Adelaide bands (2026)
sections.summary: Cosmetic (new doors + benchtop): $15,000–$30,000. Mid (full cabinets + new stone + tile): $30,000–$55,000. High (solid-timber + stone + appliances): $55,000–$100,000+.

sections.title: Five cost drivers
sections.summary: ① Cabinet material (solid > 2-pac > moisture board); ② Benchtop (natural stone > engineered > laminate); ③ Moving plumbing/power; ④ Demolition; ⑤ Project size (partial vs full strip).

sections.title: Holding the budget
sections.summary: ① Keep existing plumbing points (one move ~$500–800); ② Engineered stone is ~half natural stone, similar durability; ③ Replace doors only, keep boxes; ④ Avoid structural changes.

insights.title: Heritage timber restoration: how it differs from ordinary renovation
insights.summary: Heritage timber repair is not just technical — it carries legal compliance and preservation duty. Why it needs a specialist team, and what SA rules apply.
insights.lead: Many 1920–1950s Adelaide homes use traditional timber and hand joinery. Restoring them takes both skill and heritage awareness.

sections.title: Heritage listing and the rules
sections.summary: In SA, buildings on the State or Local Heritage Register need Heritage Approval (Section 49 permit) with a heritage-architect-reviewed method before timber repair starts.

sections.title: Traditional joinery demands
sections.summary: Mortise-and-tenon needs hand work not modern connectors; timber must match the original species and era; surface systems must follow period paint (lime wash, milk paint).

sections.title: MEL ONE heritage experience
sections.summary: Our joiners know Adelaide period forms (Federation Bungalow, Inter-War Californian Bungalow) and deliver compliant, faithful restoration.

insights.title: Solid vs engineered timber flooring: which suits your home?
insights.summary: Solid and engineered timber each have trade-offs. The right pick balances budget, floor level, moisture and look.
insights.lead: Timber flooring is among the most-used surfaces in a home. The wrong choice costs heavily in repair; the right one lifts comfort and value.

sections.title: Solid timber pros & cons
sections.summary: Pros: natural grain, multiple sandings (100-year life), value. Cons: dearer, moisture-sensitive, pro install, not ideal on damp ground floors.

sections.title: Engineered timber pros & cons
sections.summary: Pros: ~60–70% of solid price, stable (less movement), straight onto slab, DIY-able. Cons: limited refinish (1–2 times), less warm sound.

sections.title: Adelaide recommendation
sections.summary: Ground floor: engineered (stable in moisture). Upper floors: budget-dependent. High budget + long value: solid (Blackwood, Jarrah). Wet areas (bath, laundry): hybrid flooring instead.

insights.title: Commercial fitout, step by step: from design to opening
insights.summary: Restaurant, café, office or retail timber fitout is a complex job of design, fire and code compliance and program. Here is the full flow and key timing.
insights.lead: A failed fitout costs more than money — it delays opening and dents the brand. Know the flow and you control risk.

sections.title: Stage 1 — Design & partners
sections.summary: Engage designer/architect → our joinery team details → coordinate fire engineer → submit DA (with heritage approval if needed). Typically 4–8 weeks.

sections.title: Stage 2 — Build & install
sections.summary: Workshop build (6–8 wks) → strip-out & base works → joinery install (2–3 wks) → paint/finish → hardware. Typically 8–12 weeks.

sections.title: Stage 3 — Handover & open
sections.summary: Building compliance → fire inspection → (food) health inspection → pre-open clean → soft furnishings. Usually 2–3 weeks after joinery.

sections.title: Timeline summary
sections.summary: Total ~16–26 weeks (4–6 months). A full fitout with DA is 2–3× a home job; start planning 6+ months out.

faqs.question: What kind of company is MEL ONE?
faqs.answer: We are a local Adelaide full-spectrum timber company covering three areas: ① on-site structural carpentry (house framing, outdoor living, fix-out, formwork, commercial fitout); ② workshop fine joinery (custom cabinetry, architectural joinery, storage, timber doors/windows/furniture); ③ restoration & maintenance (termite repair, heritage carpentry, floor restoration). We are not a single subcontractor — we are a one-stop partner taking your project from structural frame to finished piece.

faqs.question: Which Adelaide areas do you service?
faqs.answer: Our core coverage is the Adelaide metropolitan area — City, North Adelaide, East and West Adelaide, the beachside suburbs (Glenelg, Henley Beach, Semaphore and more) and the Hills. Regional SA projects can be discussed by location; tell us where the job is.

faqs.question: Are you licensed for building work in SA?
faqs.answer: Yes. MEL ONE holds a South Australian Building Work Contractor Licence issued by Consumer and Business Services (CBS). Our structural carpentry is carried out within licence scope and to the SA Building Rules.

faqs.question: Do you work with builders?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. We support house-and-land builders (carpentry subcontracting), renovation builders (kitchen/bath cabinetry supply and install) and commercial builders (fitout, formwork). We know AS 1684 framing and mainstream Australian build systems and slot into builder teams seamlessly.

faqs.question: What does custom cabinetry cost?
faqs.answer: Price depends on material, size and detail. Adelaide 2026 reference (cabinets only, no benchtops): standard 2-pac MDF $8,000–$18,000; mid composite $15,000–$30,000; solid/high-end (Blackwood, American Oak) $30,000–$60,000+. We give a written quote after measure, with a free preliminary assessment and 3D design.

faqs.question: How is decking priced?
faqs.answer: Driven by material and scope. Adelaide reference: Treated Pine $180–$280/m²; Merbau $280–$400/m²; Spotted Gum $320–$450/m²; base works and waterproofing add $2,000–$5,000. Confirmed after site check.

faqs.question: Do you give free quotes?
faqs.answer: Yes — a free preliminary assessment and quote guidance. Simple jobs (one furniture piece, small repair) get a phone/photo estimate; complex jobs (kitchen reno, structural carpentry, commercial fitout) get an on-site measure and a detailed written quote valid 30 days.

faqs.question: What does termite damage repair cost?
faqs.answer: Depends on extent and whether structure is involved: local jamb/floor replace $1,500–$5,000; partial frame repair (1–2 nodes) $5,000–$15,000; wide frame replace + barrier $15,000–$50,000+; engineer's report adds $1,500–$3,000. Act early — we coordinate a licensed pest controller to limit spread.

faqs.question: Can you do heritage building restoration?
faqs.answer: Yes. Our joiners know Adelaide period forms (Federation Bungalow, Inter-War Californian Bungalow, Georgian/Victorian) and their timber character and repair craft. For heritage-listed buildings we prepare a compliant method under the SA Heritage Act and obtain Heritage Approval before work.

faqs.question: How long from kitchen measure to install?
faqs.answer: Full kitchen reno (measure to install): standard cabinetry build 6–8 weeks; strip-out & base 1–2 weeks; install 1–2 weeks; finish & tune 3–5 days — about 10–14 weeks. Solid-timber cabinets may take 14–18 weeks for material lead. We give a dated program with clear milestones.

faqs.question: Do you take on commercial fitouts?
faqs.answer: Yes. We deliver timber fitouts for Adelaide venues (restaurants, cafés, bars — partitions, feature ceilings, bars, displays), offices (partition walls, meeting feature walls, reception) and retail (brand walls, custom furniture), plus hotels and clinics. On large jobs we work with the head contractor as carpentry subcontractor.

faqs.question: Can I see completed projects?
faqs.answer: Yes. With client consent we publish case studies (photos + description) on our projects page. For a specific type (kitchen, heritage, commercial fitout) we can arrange a visit where possible — Adelaide-local clients first.

faqs.question: How long for custom solid-timber furniture (e.g. a dining table)?
faqs.answer: Design sign-off 1–2 weeks; timber sourcing/drying (if specific size/species) 2–4 weeks; machining & assembly 2–3 weeks; finish (sand, oil/paint) 1 week — about 6–10 weeks. Local Blackwood/Jarrah can run longer on supply; imported Oak is usually quicker. Confirmed at quote.

faqs.question: What warranty and quality assurance do you provide?
faqs.answer: Structural carpentry: 6-year structural warranty per SA building law. Fine joinery/cabinetry: 2-year workmanship & material warranty. Floor & deck oiling: 1-year workmanship. Restoration: 1-year workmanship. All cover workmanship defects; material faults follow each supplier's warranty. Full terms are in the contract.

faqs.question: How do you manage site safety and cleanliness?
faqs.answer: We run SWMS (Safe Work Method Statement): site risk assessment before start; barrier and signage; daily site clean; waste sorted and removed at completion; all workers hold White Card + insurance. On commercial fitouts we coordinate hours (after-hours/weekends) with the head contractor to minimise trading disruption.

faqs.question: How do I book a site assessment or quote?
faqs.answer: Three ways: ① the contact form on our Contact page; ② phone 0403 202 949; ③ email handymanfelix.au2026@outlook.com. We reply within 24 hours. When booking, please note project type (kitchen reno / new home framing / decking / heritage repair), suburb, rough budget and preferred start — so we send the right person.
